taskVersion.name: ves-heldout-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station H-05 (survey area H). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 26.6 | 4.30 | 4.30
2 | 119.1 | 2.37 | 6.67
3 | 340.4 | 0.77 | 7.44
4 | 640.3 | 0.77 | 8.21
5 | 2441.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as AAA-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: H-05
Curve type: A-type (resistivities increase monotonically with depth: 26.6 → 119.1 → 340.4 → 640.3 → 2441.4 Ω·m; the "AAA-type" label on file is not a standard VES classification and should be corrected to A-type)
Aquifer depth: 4.30 – 6.67 m (Layer 2, moderate resistivity ~119.1 Ω·m, interpreted as a saturated weathered/fractured zone overlying increasingly resistive, likely unweathered bedrock below)

Recommendation: Target the 4.30–6.67 m interval as the primary water-bearing zone, with casing set through the top ~4.3 m of low-resistivity overburden; given the sharp resistivity increase below 7.4 m (indicative of competent bedrock), plan for minimal productive yield beyond ~8 m and be prepared to terminate drilling if hard, dry rock is encountered.
